items.title: Add `uv license` or similar to audit dependency licenses
items.reason: The closest license-specific issue asks how uv could obtain dependency license fields or classifiers and whether to record them in `uv.lock`. It targets a dedicated audit command rather than CycloneDX output, so it does not supersede this request.

items.title: Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) output
items.reason: The canonical parent discussion chose a lockfile-based CycloneDX `uv export` format and defined an initially minimal SBOM. It was completed without a license-specific requirement.

items.title: Add SBOM export support
items.reason: This implemented CycloneDX 1.5 export for astral-sh/uv#6012. The resulting exporter constructs components without licenses, while current lock package metadata contains dependency requirements and extras but no license field.

items.title: `uv export --format cyclonedx1.5` omits component hashes that `uv.lock` already carries
items.reason: This is the closest analogous CycloneDX enrichment request. Maintainers treated adding omitted hashes as an enhancement because the initial implementation deferred them; unlike licenses, those hashes already existed in `uv.lock`. It was fixed by astral-sh/uv#21131.

items.title: Include hashes in cyclonedx exports
items.reason: This shows how optional component data was added after the initial exporter, but it could directly reuse artifact hashes already stored in the lockfile; license support requires an additional metadata-source decision.

related.search_scope: Literal searches covered `cyclonedx license`, `SBOM license`, `component license`, `license information`, `license field`, `uv export license`, `Metadata23 license`, and `License-Expression`. Conceptual searches covered dependency-license auditing, package and license metadata, classifiers, `uv.lock` storage, SBOM component metadata, indexes, and direct-URL metadata. Fix-oriented searches covered all issue states and open, closed, and merged pull requests for the original CycloneDX implementation and later missing-field fixes. No earlier tracker for licenses in CycloneDX output was found. astral-sh/uv#8156 was the most plausible duplicate but was ruled out because it requests a separate license-audit interface; astral-sh/uv#21122 differs because its hashes were already present in `uv.lock`.

type_reason: This requests optional component metadata that the existing lockfile-based exporter has never populated. The implementation explicitly leaves component licenses unset, and the lock model retains dependency requirements, extras, and groups rather than license metadata. Supporting it therefore requires a new metadata acquisition and fallback policy rather than correcting a regression. astral-sh/uv#21617 is also currently labeled `enhancement`.
summary: No duplicate was found. astral-sh/uv#8156 concerns the same license-metadata acquisition problem but requests a dedicated audit command. astral-sh/uv#6012 and astral-sh/uv#16523 established the minimal CycloneDX exporter, while astral-sh/uv#21122 and astral-sh/uv#21131 provide an analogous but simpler enrichment precedent.
draft_response: Thanks for raising this. The CycloneDX exporter introduced in astral-sh/uv#16523 currently leaves component licenses unset, and `uv.lock` package metadata does not retain license fields, so this is more than wiring an existing lockfile value into the output. astral-sh/uv#8156 is related, but it tracks a dedicated dependency-license audit command rather than CycloneDX enrichment, so this should remain a separate enhancement. The next design step is to define authoritative sources and fallbacks for PEP 639 license expressions, legacy license fields or classifiers, and registry, direct-URL, and local packages—especially whether export may perform additional index requests or artifact downloads when the lockfile lacks that metadata.
